resolutions.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2028 = target completion/start-up of MGS Expansion Phase 3 (MGS-3), which the EWPS-1-Shedgum '4' segment belongs to. Blackridge explicitly states 'Project Completion Date: Q4 2028' and identifies Package 3 as laying 56-inch pipelines EWGP-3 and EWGP-4 from EWPS-1 to Shedgum (56km) in Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia, owned by Saudi Aramco. SPA (official Saudi Press Agency) and OGJ 25bn-contract-awards articles both independently reference the 2028 timeline for the strategic gas expansion. Three independent sources support 2028. Original Aramco press release (aramco.com/.../25bn-contract-awards) timed out on verification (ReadTimeout) so was dropped in favor of the SPA/OGJ reprints/originals of the same announcement.

StartCountryOrArea and EndCountryOrArea = Saudi Arabia. Both endpoints (Shedgum gas plant and EWPS-1) are in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia. Blackridge locates the project in 'Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia'; MEED describes the Shedgum-to-EWPS-1 Master Gas System expansion segments, all in Saudi Arabia. Two independent sources agree.

SegmentCost=$46,000,000 USD is an INFERRED per-pipeline half-split, not a directly stated figure. The Gas Arabian Services EPC contract for 'Master Gas System expansion from SHEDGUM to EWPS-1' is $92 million (SAR 344,614,412), covering two parallel 56-inch pipelines EWGP-3 and EWGP-4 (Blackridge: 'Lay 56-inch pipelines EWGP-3 and EWGP-4 from EWPS-1 to Shedgum'). This segment row is pipeline '4' only, so $92M / 2 = $46M. Zawya (from the Tadawul/Argaam disclosure) and MEED independently report the $92M Shedgum-EWPS-1 award. FLAG: the $46M is GEM's allocation of the shared two-pipe contract; no source states $46M for pipeline 4 alone. Tier medium because the underlying $92M contract is well-sourced but the split is an assumption.

Owner1=Aramco 100%. Saudi Aramco is the project owner/developer of the Master Gas System Expansion Phase 3; the Gas Arabian EPC awards for the Shedgum-EWPS-1 segment name Saudi Aramco as the awarding owner. Zawya, MEED, and Blackridge all independently name Saudi Aramco as owner. Aramco press release (aramco.com/.../25bn-contract-awards) timed out on verification and was replaced by these three.
